**Sound, images and stored recordings in a process; slots shared across deployments; waits a loop can come back to.**

**2026-10-26.** Engine 0.6.0 lets a process work with audio, images and recordings kept in an
object store, share a limited number of slots across deployments, end a session before its
instance ends, and wait at the same node as many times as a loop brings it there.

The book's **[What's new in 0.6](https://sutra.startr.trade/whats-new-0-6.html)** page lists every
feature with a walkthrough you can run on your own machine against the bundled stub model server
— no provider key needed.

There is no new BPMN element. One value joins the `q:` vocabulary, additively:
`<q:audit capture="media">`.

## Preview in this release

**Live audio sessions** (`AudioSession`, `require: [realtime]`, the OpenAI Realtime and Gemini
Live adapters) and **video understanding** (clips, sampled frames and images) are **preview**.
They were run against the real Gemini and OpenAI APIs on 2026-10-26, as well as against
in-process stand-ins of the provider APIs, and stay preview: their shapes may still change. Audio
on a turn-based call — `audio`, `audioOutput`, `voice: pipeline` — is not preview.

### Verified against the live provider APIs

Run on 2026-10-26 with `examples/ai-advanced/live-check.sh` against the real provider APIs:

- **Gemini** (13 passed, 0 failed): summaries (sync, streamed and async), an image, video frames,
  a video clip, audio understanding, structured JSON, a media reference read from an object
  store, a refused reference with the wrong sha256, Live round trips with server turn detection
  (`gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest`) and with manual turns (`gemini-3.8-live`), and no
  credential in any URL.
- **OpenAI** (12 passed, 0 failed): summaries (sync, streamed and async), JSON mode, a polled
  background job, audio understanding with a spoken answer, the voice pipeline, a media
  reference, a refused reference with the wrong sha256, and Realtime round trips with manual and
  with server turn detection (`gpt-realtime`); the key went in no URL.
- **Not run in this pass:** the OpenAI webhook job (it needs a public tunnel), and Anthropic
  fallback, tool calls and batch (no Anthropic key).
- **Known limit:** `gemini-3.8-live`'s voice-activity detection heard only the first word of the
  synthetic sample question, while a recorded human voice worked; the book's *Live audio
  sessions* section describes this.

## Audio in model calls

A user turn may carry `audio` (`{data, format}`, the format written as a media type such as
`audio/wav`, `audio/L16;rate=16000`, `audio/PCMU`), and `audioOutput` asks for a spoken answer.
The reply adds `audio`, `transcript` and `audioPreserved`. The `llm` transport converts between
the call's formats and the provider's in pure Rust (WAV, G.711 µ-law / A-law, resampling). A
candidate that cannot take what the call carries is skipped: the audio is never silently dropped
for a text-only model.

- **`voice: pipeline`** runs speech-to-text, a text model and text-to-speech through an
  `llm.speech` provider, for models that take no audio.
- **`require:`** gains `audio-input`, `audio-output`, `audio-understanding`,
  `video-understanding` and `realtime`, and now applies to every call on the channel.
- **Native `gemini` provider** (`sutra-llm-gemini`, bundled in the image): Gemini's own API, which
  carries audio, images and video that the compatible `google-gemini` route cannot.
- **Structured answers:** a call with `json: true` gets the parsed answer under `json`, so a flow
  reads its fields directly; when it does not parse, `jsonError` says why (for example, cut off at
  `max-output-tokens`, which a reasoning model's thinking also counts against).

## Media references and object stores

A process need never hold the media it works on. Named object stores are declared in the engine
configuration (`sutra.object-stores.<name>`, S3-compatible, with optional envelope encryption at
rest). A media part on a model call may give `{ref: <object URI>, sha256}` instead of inline data;
the channel reads it from its `llm.media-store`, checks the digest and size, and sends it on. A
reference that cannot be honoured — outside the store, missing, too large, the wrong digest — is a
permanent `SUTRA.LLM.MEDIA.REFUSED`, and an HTTP caller that sent it gets `422` with that code.

- **`<q:audit capture="media">`**: audit events carry the media *references* found among the
  instance's variables, never the media.
- **Erasure and retention delete recordings.** Subject erasure and terminal retention delete the
  referenced objects and amend the audit events to say so. A recording that cannot be deleted is
  never skipped: erasure fails for that instance and retention retries.
- **`sutra-objectstore`** (new crate): the `ObjectStore` seam with an S3 Signature V4 client, an
  in-memory store, sealed objects, multipart uploads, ranged reads and paginated listings.

## Capacity pools and session end

**Capacity pools** are named, cluster-wide slot counts declared in the engine configuration
(`sutra.capacity-pools.<name>`) and drawn from by inbound and outbound channels of any deployment
(`pool: <name>`), with per-direction reserves and a tenant allow-list. A full pool answers an
inbound start `503 SUTRA.INBOUND.POOL.EXHAUSTED` and holds an outbound request in the outbox,
oldest first, without counting an attempt. One slot is held per active call, so an instance
bridging two legs holds two.

**`session-end:`** on an inbound channel ends an instance's session — releasing its
`max-concurrent-instances` slot and its pool slots — when a correlated message arrives or when the
flow replies, while the instance runs on.

## Waiting at the same node again

A loop that brings the token back to a message catch, receive task, user task, channel call, timer
or event-based gateway now parks a **new** wait each time round, with its own timer, timeout,
retry budget and correlation keys. A late message for a past round no longer resumes the instance.
A resume continues from the satisfied wait instead of replaying the graph from the start, so
nothing upstream runs again, and the instance's audit history reads round by round.

## For transport authors

- **Model channels other transports can call.** The `llm` transport publishes every live
  `mode: call` channel to a process-wide registry (`llm_channels()`), so a media transport opens
  model calls and live sessions through a named channel of its deployment — with that channel's
  candidates, fallback, `require:`, key references and concurrency limit.
- **Transports write audit events** to an instance's or a deployment's journal
  (`sutra_channels::transport_audit()`), under the instance's `<q:audit>` level and redaction. The
  instance history now pages losslessly by a journal `ordinal` (`?afterOrdinal=`); `?afterSeq=`
  keeps working.

## Telephony and video

Telephony, IVRs, meetings and WebRTC are not part of this engine. They live in the separate
open-source repository [sutra-voice](https://github.com/startr-trade/sutra-voice), which consumes
this engine as a submodule and builds on the pieces above.

## Security

- The Gemini API key is never put in a URL: a live session mints a single-use ephemeral token and
  sends it in the `Authorization` header. URLs printed in failures have their query values and
  user-info blanked.
- `SUTRA_CRYPTO_MASTER_KEY` is resolved as a secret reference (`env:`, `secret:`, `vault:`, …), as
  every other secret is.

## Fixed

- An event-based gateway resumed by its winning arm continues along that arm.
- A relay resumes the wait the instance is parked at when several waits share a channel, and is
  refused (`SUTRA.RUNTIME.RESUME.NOT_WAITING`) when it names a wait the instance is not parked at.
- A wait node's own `<q:alias>` is indexed when it parks; a relay correlates through a start-event
  alias even when the wait binds its payload under another name.
- A parallel join inside a loop waits for a full set of tokens each time round.
- The admin instance endpoints inspect an instance whose sensitive variables are encrypted at rest.
- Tenant-wide subject erasure covers deployments loaded from a watched directory.
- `sutra lint` no longer reports a resume-only or `session-end` channel as inert.

## Upgrading

Four migrations run at boot: V202 and V203 on the audit journal, V703 and V704 for capacity pools.
The snapshot format is unchanged, and instances parked by a 0.5 engine resume under the new rules.
Behaviour changes to be aware of:

- **A dead-lettered HTTP inbound answers its cause.** It used to answer
  `500 SUTRA.INBOUND.NON_IDEMPOTENT_FAILURE`; it now answers the cause's code and message, with the
  incident under `incident`, and `422` when an extension registers the code as the caller's fault.
- **`SUTRA_CRYPTO_MASTER_KEY`** is read as a secret reference. A literal value is still accepted as
  the raw key (with a warning at boot), so data encrypted under it stays readable; an
  unresolvable reference refuses to boot.
- **`require:` on an `llm` channel** applies to every call on the channel.
- **A resume no longer replays the graph.** Listeners no longer see `NODE_ENTERED` / `NODE_LEFT`
  for nodes in front of a resumed wait, and the wait itself now records `NODE_LEFT`.
- A channel with `pool:` always takes the outbox path, even with `ack-mode: on-complete`.

## Examples

Three new example packages, each with a walkthrough in the book: `examples/media-recordings`
(media references, audited by reference, deleted on erasure and retention),
`examples/capacity-pools` (shared slots, sessions that end early) and `examples/review-loop` (a
process that waits at the same nodes round after round). `examples/ai-advanced` gains voice,
voice-pipeline and vision flows, and its `live-check.sh` covers every native Gemini path.

## Install

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/startr-trade/sutra:0.6.0
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/startr-trade/sutra/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.6.0
```

The library crates are on crates.io as `sutra-feel = "0.6.0"` and `sutra-dmn = "0.6.0"`.
